description:
FOUND s500 (Fable, 2026-09-28) while preparing the everyday-singles brief; #2084 (4) had attributed the Archive::Tar row to the stash walk -- WRONG: `keys %{"Archive::Tar::Constant::"}` DOES list the constants under PCL (probed: A,B,MODE,f for a package with two constants and a sub; only SCALAR/ARRAY names are missing from the snapshot).  The miss is prototype().

PROBES (perl 5.40.3 vs main 209e7533; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/tmp/proto2.pl, constproto.pl, atc.pl):
    use constant MODE => 1; sub protoed ($$) {1} sub plain {1} sub empty () {1} sub attr :prototype($) {1} my $anon = sub ($) {1};
    prototype(\&MODE)      perl ''     PCL undef
    prototype(\&protoed)   perl '$$'   PCL undef        (same for prototype("protoed") by name, and cross-package via X->can($n))
    prototype(\&plain)     perl undef  PCL undef        (right)
    prototype(\&empty)     perl ''     PCL undef
    prototype(\&attr)      perl '$'    PCL '$'          (the ONLY registered spelling)
    prototype($anon)       perl '$'    PCL undef
    use Archive::Tar::Constant; scalar(@Archive::Tar::Constant::EXPORT)   perl 49   PCL 0   -> `use Archive::Tar` dies at the first MODE call.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-__pcl_set_prototype` / `%pcl-sub-prototypes` (the registry, weak on the function object) and `p-prototype` (whose docstring states the gap); the `:prototype` attribute desugar in Pl/Parser.pm ~1139 emits `__pcl_set_prototype(\&f, '$')` after the sub -- the classic prototype and `use constant` need the SAME emission (rule 11: one registrar; a `use constant` sub registers ''; an anonymous `sub ($) {}` wraps its lambda the way the anonymous `:prototype` form already does, Pl/PExpr.pm ~3309).  The compile-time consumption of the prototype (parse facts, `_proto_parse_spec`) is unchanged -- this only ADDS the run-time record.
THE ENTRY'S CONDITION: docs/not-supported.md "## `prototype()` -- returns only registered prototypes" says "registering every prototyped sub is easy but changes `defined prototype(...)` guards in code that works today; do it deliberately (with a sweep) or not at all.  No maintained CPAN module reads its own classic prototypes back at runtime."  The second sentence is false (core Archive::Tar::Constant does, and so does any Exporter-by-stash-walk idiom); the first names the bar: the FULL SWEEP + the CPAN board legs that `use constant`-heavy dists reach, and every `defined prototype(...)` guard in lib/ + the corpus read (grep `prototype(` over lib/, cpan-tests/, perl-tests/ -- list the sites and what each does when the answer changes from undef to a string).  The entry is REWRITTEN in the same commit (perl-exact, or the residue that stays).
BAR: emission change => gen bump + artifacts; corpus-diff (every file with a classic prototype or a `use constant` gains a registration form -- ONE class, or make it a compile-time table load so the per-sub emission is a single extra form); the full sweep; companion op/cproto.t + comp/proto.t + op/sub.t + lib/ legs; the everyday line (modules/Archive-Tar-Compress must turn `same` -- and then its NEXT differing line, if any, is measured, not guessed); guard rows in Pl/t/core-proto-01.t's file or the sub-family file, inverse-verified.  Perf: a hash insert per sub DEFINITION (not per call) -- measure the `use Moo` / Sub::Quote path (string-eval'd subs are definitions too) on the `moo-objs` bench row, FLAG > 1 %.


=== DONE (s500a, Opus, 2026-09-30) ===
THE CENSUS the not-supported entry asked for (every `prototype(` reader): in-tree -- perl-tests/signatures.t (95 `is prototype(\&tNNN), undef` on SIGNATURE subs: unchanged, a signature registers nothing; plus the commented-out t000 row, which now passes), lib/Sub/Util.pm (reads the registry -- gains), cpan-tests Test-Simple t/Legacy/subtest/plan.t (`prototype('subtest')` undef: PCL's subtest is the runtime TAP layer, unchanged).  Core modules PCL loads: Archive::Tar::Constant:117 (the target: `defined … and not length …` now keeps the constants -> @EXPORT 49 = perl), Memoize:164 + Test2::Mock:226/258/268 (copy a sub's prototype onto a wrapper: now perl's text), Fatal.pm:1317/1392 (autodie reads user prototypes: now perl's text), Net/Ping.pm:66 (`defined prototype \&{$name} ? sub () {$value} : sub {$value}` -- a constant's '' now takes the `sub ()` branch, as in perl).  No guard found whose behaviour becomes WRONG when undef turns into perl's string.
THE EMISSION (zero extra forms per definition): the p-sub FACTS plist already had a `:prototype "TEXT"` key (#1035); the p-sub MACRO now registers it right after installing the function (`p-__pcl_set_prototype`, the ONE registrar) -- at DEFINITION, so an earlier statement or a `\&f` taken before the sub sees it (p-prototype follows a late-binding trampoline to its target).  ONE reading of the text, `Pl::Parser::sub_proto_text`, feeds both printers (Parser2 `_sub_facts`, v1 `_process_sub_statement`); `use constant` prints `(:prototype "")`.  An attribute's record (from_attr, now carrying its raw text) wins over an inline prototype or a signature, is never overwritten by the definition's scan (both pipelines), and travels with the lexsub rename.  The named-sub `__pcl_set_prototype(\&f, …)` STATEMENT the attribute pre-pass used to splice after the sub is DELETED (one path).  Anonymous `sub ($) {…}`: the anonymous-sub handler in PExpr (which already consumed the Token::Prototype) wraps the func_ref in `__pcl_set_prototype(…, 'TEXT')`.  TEXT is perl's: between the parens, WHITESPACE KEPT (`sub f ( $ ; $ )` answers ' $ ; $ ', probed).  Where signatures are in force every paren list is a signature (no prototype).
FOUND BEHIND IT (the row's NEXT differing line, measured): core Archive::Tar called `$entry->$_()` -- ExprToCL's dynamic-method test compared `ref eq 'PPI::Token::Symbol'` and `$_` is a Token::Magic, so it called a method literally named "$_".  Fixed (isa).  The row's next cause after that: IO::Zlib->new TIES *$fh (tie on a filehandle, #155), so reading the tar back dies -- the baseline row is re-attributed to #155; the row is NOT `same`.
PROBES: proto2.pl, constproto.pl, proto3.pl, ws.pl, atc.pl, lexproto.pl -- all = perl (base: undef everywhere but the attribute).  Found and filed: #2542 (a FILE-level `my sub NAME :prototype(…)` glues the name).
GUARDS: Pl/t/core-proto-01.t rows 12-15 (+ row 10 rewritten under the four-conjunct rule: it asserted the gap), Pl/t/misc-fixes-01.t `$o->$_()` row, Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t (the "prints ()" row now uses a signature sub; + a constant `(:prototype "")` row), Pl/t/constants-01.t shape rows updated.
COMPANION (--jobs 1, A/B vs a 1bae682b extraction, 18 files): op/cproto.t 254/0 both; comp/proto.t 63/32 -> 75/20, op/lexsub.t 78/63 -> 80/61, op/attrproto.t 17/31 -> 18/30, op/signatures.t 915/296 -> 916/295 (spliced); op/sub.t and the rest identical.  comp/proto.t's snapshot (78/38) was already stale at 558cc5a0 -- #2543.
CORPUS: 16 of 111 files + 1 shape differ, every hunk a `:prototype` fact, the deleted attribute statement, or an anonymous `sub (&)` wrap.  not-supported.md entry REWRITTEN (perl-exact + the residue: bare-name record collision, no "Prototype mismatch" warning); ir-spec §5.1 FACTS normative.
subject: Run-time `prototype()` answers undef for a CLASSIC prototype (`sub f ($$)`), for every `use constant` sub (perl: '') and for an anonymous `sub ($) {}` -- only the `:prototype()` attribute registers; not-supported.md's own condition for closing the gap ('do it deliberately, with a sweep') is now MET because core Archive::Tar::Constant reads its constants' prototypes back at run time (`_list_consts`: `defined prototype($sub) and not length prototype($sub)`), so `@EXPORT` is EMPTY under PCL and the everyday row modules/Archive-Tar-Compress dies 'Undefined subroutine &Archive::Tar::File::MODE'
